title: 📝 Section 4 — Lecture Note-Taking

sections.heading: Section 4 format
sections.body:
Section 4 is the hardest — a single academic lecture or talk with no pauses. Question types include:
• Note/summary completion
• Table completion
• Multiple choice
• Short answer

You're essentially taking lecture notes under exam conditions. The vocabulary is academic and specialist.

sections.heading: Abbreviation system
sections.body:
You need a personal shorthand for fast note-taking:
• → = leads to / causes
• ↑ = increase   ↓ = decrease
• ∴ = therefore   ∵ = because
• w/ = with   w/o = without
• e.g. = for example   i.e. = that is
• govt = government   env = environment
• c. = approximately

Develop YOUR OWN system and practise it consistently.

highlight: In Section 4, you won't understand every word — that's normal. Keep writing. A partial answer may still be correct. Never stop to think about a word you missed.

question: In Section 4 note-completion, you hear "...which ultimately led to a dramatic reduction in biodiversity across the region." The gap is: "Result: dramatic _______ in biodiversity". What do you write?
explanation:
"Reduction" is correct — it's a NOUN to follow "dramatic" and fill the noun phrase "dramatic _____ in biodiversity".

Always check the grammatical category required:
• After "dramatic" → noun or adjective
• "Reduction" (noun) ✅  "Reduce" (verb) ❌
• The answer must fit the slot grammatically

instruction: Match each abbreviation to its meaning:
explanation: Building a fast abbreviation system lets you keep pace with Section 4 lectures. Practise using these symbols when watching any educational video — make it automatic before test day.

question: The lecture mentions: "...three main causes: industrial pollution, which is the primary driver; agricultural runoff; and, to a lesser extent, urban development." The question asks: "What is identified as the PRIMARY cause?" What do you write?
explanation:
"Primary driver" = main/most important cause.

The lecturer explicitly signals importance: "the primary driver". In Section 4, always listen for:
• "The main/primary/key..."
• "Most importantly..."
• "Above all..."
• "The principal factor..."
